title: Enterprise priority lanes for model onboarding and deprecation visibility
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are requesting predictable onboarding lanes for new model variants, version pin requests, and clearer deprecation timelines tied to guaranteed eval windows. Current catalog intake is noisy for enterprise requests and lacks observable SLAs or a path for temporary pin exemptions during compliance or performance regressions.

Scope: Define refined priority lanes (fast-path, standard, regulated) for model adds and pin/deprecation requests; implement visibility surfaces in the Console and Catalog UI; design an ‘exception pin’ flow with audit logging and time-boxed exemptions; and add a shadow-eval thermalization window for any fast-path onboarding to catch regressions before full traffic shifts.

Deliverables:
- Intake rubric for enterprise lanes with scoring weights and SLA targets.
- Catalog metadata fields for lane, pin-exemption-token, and deprecation-notice-url.
- Console dashboard mockups for lane occupancy, outstanding pins, and deprecation calendar.
- Shadow-eval toggle and thermalization window implementation plan for engineers.
- Documentation (Confluence + customer-facing KB) for how to request, escalate, and audit pins/deprecations.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement the full backend enforcer for hard-deprecation blocking (separate ENG epic). Not addressing pricing changes in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: A lane rubric doc exists with scoring weights and example enterprise scenarios
Console mockups show lane assignment and deprecation calendar for catalog entries
Catalog metadata schema updated to include lane and pin-exemption fields (proposal linked)
Shadow-eval thermalization window defined and ops runbook created
Customer KB and internal PRD published with request templates and escalation path

2025-02-21 - Design review: Danika Morales approved console layout but recommended a compact lane indicator and an explicit 'pin history' flyout. See Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Model-Catalog-Lanes
2025-02-24 - Decision: implement time-boxed pin exemptions (default 30d) with optional extension requests; require KMS-backed audit entries for each exemption (security requested).

2025-02-27 - Trade-off note: fast-path (24h SLA) will run limited shadow-evals for first 10k tokens to reduce regression risk; adds ~0.8% cost per fast-path onboarding. Ops accepted the cost for enterprise lanes.
2025-03-01 - Action: Drafted PRD and customer KB: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f
2025-03-02 - Eng update (ENG-11740): prototyping shadow-eval toggle and thermalization window; opened GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/842
2025-03-03 - Stakeholder feedback: Legal asked to add deprecation notice minimum 60 days for regulated customers; added as optional field on metadata and escalation path required for shorter windows.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Shadow-eval scope: customers in fast-path will see faster onboarding but fewer early traffic samples; thermalization window balances speed and safety.
Pin exemptions: time-boxed with audit trail to minimize long-term sprawl in catalog; long-term pins should convert to formal sponsorship lanes.
Visibility: Console will surface lane occupancy and upcoming deprecations to reduce surprise for platform teams.
Rollout plan: pilot with 3 enterprise customers, monitor regressions for 4 weeks, iterate before wider roll-out.
